why: Until now nobody could tell whether the live system was healthy: request logs were empty, the health page always said healthy, errors went unseen, there was no backup you could restore, and any logged-in user could use administrator-only endpoints. A shop that takes customers' money needs to find out about a problem before the customer does, recover from a bad day, and control who can do what.
approach: Health pages that really check the database and schema, a metrics page for a dashboard, WhatsApp alerts to the owner for the five things that need a person, error reporting that strips personal data, a request id on every log line, indexes for the slow queries, administrator and token controls on logins, and scripts for backup, restore drill and a safe release.

decisions.decision: Hand-roll a small Prometheus-format metrics page instead of adding a metrics library.
decisions.why: No new dependency to download or audit; the needed numbers are a few counters and gauges.

alternatives.why_not: A new package for a very small need; downloads were avoided.

decisions.decision: Send operations alerts to the owner's WhatsApp, one message per problem with a cooldown stored in the database.
decisions.why: The owner already watches WhatsApp. A database cooldown survives restarts and is shared by every process.

alternatives.why_not: Slower to notice; no email service is set up.
A restart would repeat every alert.

decisions.decision: Refresh tokens are single-use; using one twice (outside a short double-tap window) logs the account out everywhere.
decisions.why: A reused token means a copy exists somewhere else; revoking everything makes a stolen token useless.

alternatives.option: Reusable refresh tokens until they expire
alternatives.why_not: A stolen token works for weeks.

decisions.decision: Until an administrator is configured, the admin-only endpoints stay open to any logged-in user (with a log warning).
decisions.why: Turning the check on with nobody configured would lock the owner out of the retry endpoint. Configuring ADMIN_USERNAMES turns it on.

alternatives.why_not: Could lock the owner out of a live fix.

errors.error: Token issued in the same second as the logout cut-off was refused
errors.cause: Token timestamps are whole seconds but the cut-off had fractions, so a brand-new token compared as older.

errors.error: Reviewer: restore drill script could be pointed at the live database
errors.cause: Only a Supabase host name was blocked; pg_restore --clean drops tables.
errors.fix: The target must not equal the application's own database and its name must contain scratch, test or restore.

errors.error: Reviewer: signing up as a different-case copy of an administrator's name could gain admin rights
errors.cause: ADMIN_USERNAMES was matched case-insensitively but sign-up was case-sensitive.
errors.fix: Sign-up refuses any name whose lowercase form is an administrator's.

domains.name: Visibility
domains.goal: Know the system's health without reading code.

tasks.title: /health/ready answers 503 with a reason when the database, schema version or upload folder is wrong
tasks.verify: Stop the database and open /health/ready from the server: it says not ready and names the database. /health/live still says alive.

tasks.title: /metrics shows orders by status, daily image use, provider outcomes, pending payments and database state
tasks.verify: Open /metrics from the server after a few orders: moraa_orders and moraa_provider_calls_total have numbers.

tasks.title: The owner gets one WhatsApp message per problem (failure rate, limit nearly used, parked payments, review items, stuck orders)
tasks.verify: Set OPS_ALERT_WHATSAPP_NUMBERS and create a parked test payment: one message arrives within 5 minutes and not another for an hour. Untested against live WhatsApp.

tasks.title: Every log line of a request and of the background job it starts carries the same short request id; error reports (optional) carry no personal data
tasks.verify: Send a test photo and search the logs for its request id: tap, charge and delivery lines all share it. Sentry itself was not connected.

tasks.title: Indexes for the slow lookups (migration 0014) and paging for the analyses list
tasks.verify: Applied only to test databases. After production is upgraded, /api/analyses answers quickly with 10,000 rows.

tasks.title: Only administrators can use the retry and failure-rate endpoints; a deactivated account stops working at once
tasks.verify: Set ADMIN_USERNAMES, call the retry endpoint as an ordinary user: 403.

tasks.title: Refresh tokens are single-use, there is a logout, and reuse revokes the account's older tokens
tasks.verify: Log in, refresh once (works), refresh again 30 seconds later with the old token (refused and all sessions end).

tasks.title: A backup script (pg_dump) and a restore drill that proves wallet balances equal their ledgers
tasks.verify: Not yet run end to end: this machine has no PostgreSQL client tools. Run both on a machine that has pg_dump and write the date in docs/OPERATIONS_RUNBOOK.md.

tasks.title: A release script upgrades the database and refuses to continue unless the result is right
tasks.verify: python scripts/release.py --check-only prints what it would do and changes nothing.

tasks.title: Unused and risky settings removed or warned about (for example eager Celery in production)
tasks.verify: Start with ENVIRONMENT=production and the default payment link: a warning names the setting.
